cues.en: In this video, we'll take a look at the Hyperloop, the brand new method of transport brought forth by the entrepreneur and billionaire Elon Musk. But it would be for a fifth mode of transport. I have a name for it, a name for it, which is called the Hyperloop. The Hyperloop? Hyperloop, yeah. The system is proposed to travel at an average speed of 900 kilometers an hour and at a top speed of 1,220 kilometers an hour.
cues.zh: 在这期视频中，我们将深入了解由亿万富翁创业家 Elon Musk 提出的全新交通方式——Hyperloop。但这将是第五种交通方式。我给它起了个名字，叫做 Hyperloop。Hyperloop？对，Hyperloop。该系统的平均运行速度预计可达每小时 900 公里，最高时速可达 1220 公里。

cues.en: It's very similar to an airplane on high altitudes. You have a low pressure environment inside the tube, a capsule that doesn't touch anywhere, hovers, and then because of the low pressure doesn't encounter a lot of resistance. It's also a lot faster. You can basically get from downtown LA to downtown San Francisco in 30 minutes. It's also extremely energy efficient due to solar power utilization. In fact, the Hyperloop could generate more power than it consumes as a closed system.
cues.zh: 这非常类似于高空飞行的飞机。管道内部处于低压环境，悬浮舱不接触任何表面，处于悬浮状态，由于气压极低，几乎不会遇到阻力。它的速度也快得多。你基本上可以在 30 分钟内从洛杉矶市中心到达旧金山市中心。由于利用了太阳能，它的能效也极高。事实上，作为一个封闭系统，Hyperloop 产生的电能甚至可以超过其消耗的电能。

cues.en: because you generate more power than you consume in the system. It's also much cheaper to build. It's about one tenth the cost of the proposed California high-speed railway system. This means that tickets could cost as little as $25. A thousand kilometers per hour in a vacuum tube for less than the construction costs of what is currently proposed for the high-speed rail connection. It will generate more power than it uses.
cues.zh: 因为你在系统中产生的电能比消耗的还要多。它的建造成本也要便宜得多。大约只有加州拟建高铁系统造价的十分之一。这意味着票价可能只要 25 美元。在真空管道中以每小时 1000 公里的速度飞驰，造价却比目前拟建的高铁线路还要低。它产生的电力将超过其消耗量。

cues.en: by solar panels and a ticket will only cost about 20 bucks. Yeah, and it's complete bullshit. Now, sure, the principle is fine. It's just not viable in practice. You know, it's like the solar roadways thing. It sounds great, but in reality, it's just bullshit made up by snake oil salesman or the mindlessly optimistic daydreaming of those who just don't want that bitter taste of reality.
cues.zh: 依靠太阳能电池板供电，而且一张票只要 20 块钱左右。是啊，这完全是一派胡言。没错，原理听起来没毛病。但在实际操作中根本行不通。你知道，这就像“太阳能公路”一样。听起来很棒，但实际上不过是江湖骗子编造的鬼话，或者是那些不愿面对残酷现实的人盲目乐观的白日梦。

cues.en: The first real challenge is simply the main impossible goal of building a 600 kilometer long vacuum chamber. I mean, even in the smaller version of the Hyperloop, which I could only just about stand up in, so it's about 2 meters in diameter, which has a cross section of about 3 meters squared, and if it's 600 kilometers long at 600,000 meters long, that means that the volume will be about 2 million cubic meters.
cues.zh: 第一个真正的挑战，单纯就是建造一个 600 公里长的真空室这一根本不可能实现的目标。我的意思是，即使是较小版本的 Hyperloop，我也就勉强能站直，它的直径大约是 2 米，截面积大约是 3 平方米，如果长 600 公里，也就是 60 万米长，这意味着它的体积将达到约 200 万立方米。

cues.en: So let's compare that to the world's largest vacuum chamber, shall we? Which is about 1 50th of the volume. This is NASA's space power facility near Cleveland, Ohio, and it is the world's biggest vacuum chamber. It's used to test spacecraft in the conditions of outer space. Yeah, that's the vacuum chamber that NASA uses to test their spacecraft in, and it's 50 times smaller than the smaller version of the Hyperloop.
cues.zh: 那么，我们把它和世界上最大的真空室对比一下，好吗？后者的体积大约只有它的五十分之一。这是位于俄亥俄州克利夫兰附近的 NASA 空间动力设施，也是世界上最大的真空室。它用于在模拟外层空间的环境下测试航天器。是的，这就是 NASA 用来测试航天器的真空室，而它比小号版的 Hyperloop 还要小 50 倍。

cues.en: It's used to test spacecraft in the conditions of outer space and it does that by pumping out the 30 tonnes of air in this chamber until there are about two grams left. Now there's a problem with making vacuum chambers that size and the first is they need to be quite heavy in construction. Aluminium is not the best thing, the strongest material to build a vacuum chamber out of so...
cues.zh: 它用来在外太空条件下测试航天器，做法是把舱内30吨空气抽出去，直到只剩大约两克。要造这么大的真空舱会有问题，第一个问题是结构必须相当重。铝并不是最佳选择，也不是造真空舱最强的材料，所以……

cues.en: they built outer concrete skin. So this thing can take the force that's present on the outside when it's pumped out to the conditions of outer space. Because there's a lot of atmosphere pushing on the outside about 10 tonnes per square metre. So to help you visualise it, here I have a square metre. So atmospheric pressure is equal to about 10 metres of water. So it's like 10 times this distance here.
cues.zh: 他们做了外层混凝土壳。这样它就能承受抽到外太空条件时外部产生的力。因为外面有大量大气在推，大约每平方米10吨。为了帮大家直观理解，这里我有一平方米。大气压大约相当于10米高的水柱。所以差不多是这里这个距离的10倍。

cues.en: So if I would have put 10 meters on top of my one square meter, cubic meter of water weighs about a ton. So 10 cubic meters pushing down on one square meter would give you a pressure of 10 tons pushing down on this square meter. Because there's a lot of atmosphere pushing on the outside about 10 tons per square meter. And there is absolutely nothing pushing on the inside because it's a vacuum.
cues.zh: 所以如果我在这一平方米上放10米高的水，一立方米水大约重一吨。那么10立方米压在一平方米上，就相当于有10吨压力压在这一平方米上。因为外面有大量大气在推，大约每平方米10吨。而里面完全没有东西在推，因为它是真空。

cues.en: And it also has to take the vibrational force of a 15 tonne capsule going through it at nearly the speed of sound. So the walls are about two centimetres thick, about an inch or so. Cool, so we can now do the calculations to adjust the steel required to make only the tube in this structure. And it turns out to be about the same mass as the steel in the world trade centre, which to be fair was a ginormous building.
cues.zh: 它还得承受一个15吨重的舱体以接近音速穿过时产生的振动力。所以壁厚大约两厘米，约一英寸左右。好，现在我们可以计算一下，只造这个结构里的管道需要多少钢材。结果所需钢材的质量差不多和世界贸易中心用的钢一样多，平心而论，那本来就是栋巨型建筑。

cues.en: Cool, so that would get us the steel to make the tube. Then comes the first real problem, which is expansion. Most people know that if you just have, say, bridges, you need an expansion joint in them. So let's take a look at the expansion for steel. It's about 13 parts per million per degree Celsius. So let's say the temperature range is going to be between freezing point and 40 degrees Celsius. That's basically a hot day, which means the overall length of this tube is going to vary about.
cues.zh: 好，这样我们就有了造管道的钢材。接下来是第一个真正的问题：膨胀。多数人都知道，比如桥梁，就得有伸缩缝。那我们来看看钢材的膨胀。大约是每摄氏度百万分之13。假设温度范围在冰点到40摄氏度之间。基本就是个大热天，这意味着这根管道的总长度会变化大约——

cues.en: for 500 parts per morning and that sort of thing. Which means that the overall length of the hyperloop from the coldest day to the hottest day will vary by about 300 meters. About the length of three football fields. Clearly expansion joints are necessary. Well that would be easier if you're looking at the expansion joints on a bridge.
cues.zh: 大约百万分之500，差不多就是这类数值。也就是说，从最冷的一天到最热的一天，Hyperloop的总长度会变化约300米。大约三个足球场的长度。显然，伸缩缝是必需的。不过，如果看桥上的伸缩缝，那会容易得多。

cues.en: Not so much if they're an expansion joint for a vacuum tube, because it's got to hold that vacuum almost perfectly whilst it's changing its length. So let's give them something reasonable, like a 100m segment of tubing. So the expansion difference between a hot day and a cold day there would be about 50mm, so a couple of inches.
cues.zh: 但如果这是真空管的伸缩缝，就没那么容易了，因为它必须在改变长度的同时几乎完美地保持真空。那就给它设个合理值，比如100米长的一段管道。这样热天和冷天之间的膨胀差大约会是50毫米，也就是两英寸左右。

cues.en: So you would need a joint about every one tenth of a kilometre, such that in the 600 kilometre hyperloop, you would need about 6000 moving part vacuum seals, and a failure on any one of them could be disastrous for the people inside the hyperloop. And this is of course assuming 100m segments of tubing, their current segments look to be more like...
cues.zh: 也就是说，大约每100米就需要一个接头，所以在600公里的 Hyperloop 中，需要大约6000个活动部件真空密封圈，而其中任何一个失效，对管道内的人来说都可能是灾难性的。当然，这还是假设管道每段长100米，但他们目前的管段看起来更像是……

cues.en: 10 meters or so, which would mean they would need 60,000 moving part vacuum seals on a 2 meter diameter tube. I mean, the only thing even remotely comparable in the world is the large Hadron Collider, which is, I don't know, maybe 50 kilometers or so of tubing. Albeit underground, so they're more or less a constant temperature, so they really don't have these expansion problems. And even at that, it's one hundredth of the volume of the Hyperloop.
cues.zh: 10米左右，这就意味着在直径2米的管道上，需要6万个活动部件真空密封圈。我是说，全世界唯一能勉强相提并论的只有大型强子对撞机，它大概有，我不知道，也许50公里左右的管道。尽管它在地下，温度基本恒定，所以根本没有这种膨胀问题。即便如此，它的体积也只有 Hyperloop 的百分之一。

cues.en: and it doesn't have a 15 ton capsule going through it, and while it does have a large number of seals to it, for the large part they won't be moving part seals, they'll just be static seals that all you have to do is tighten up the bolts and you're done. So how do they address this in their white paper, which is the go-to documentation for the Hyperloop?
cues.zh: 而且里面可没有一个15吨重的舱体飞驰而过，虽然它确实有大量的密封结构，但在很大程度上并不是活动密封，它们只是静态密封，只要把螺栓拧紧就行了。那么他们在白皮书——也就是 Hyperloop 最核心的技术文档中——是怎么解决这个问题的呢？

cues.en: A telescopic tube similar to the boxy ones used to access airplanes and airports would be needed at the end station to address the cumulative length change of the tube. Now that just blew my mind because that really does sound like they just intend to weld all of the tubes together. That is, they haven't done even the simplest expansion calculations. Now sure, welded tubes would be great for holding the vacuum.
cues.zh: 在终点站需要一个类似于机场登机桥那种箱式伸缩管，以应对管道累积的长度变化。这简直让我惊呆了，因为这听起来就好像他们打算把所有的管道全焊死在一起。也就是说，他们甚至连最简单的膨胀计算都没做过。当然，焊接管道在维持真空方面确实很棒。

cues.en: but it does mean that your station's going to have to move by about three football pitches between the hottest and coldest day. This station is probably the most compact station and it really the entire activity actually happens almost here. This is more still over lounge shopping area. This is where you get your magazines, your coffee. But still everything happens on the go. Not to mention how you expect the support pylons to hold all of this up and account for that movement.
cues.zh: 但这意味着在最热和最冷的日子之间，你的车站必须移动大约三个足球场的距离。“这个车站可能是最紧凑的车站，所有活动基本上都在这里进行。这更像是一个溢流休息购物区。在这里你可以买杂志、喝咖啡。但一切依旧在行进中发生。”更不用说你指望支撑塔柱怎么撑起这一切，还要去配合那种位移了。

cues.en: Plus, if you're just going to weld all of these tubes together, you're going to get massive buckling problems. Painted white or not, in the hard Californian sun, the top of these things will get hotter than the bottom. That is, the top will expand more than the bottom. And with a 500 mile long tube, you're going to get massive buckling problems of the sort that you would get on a bimetallic strip. The brass should expand more than the steel.
cues.zh: 另外，如果真要把所有管道焊在一起，就会遇到严重的屈曲变形问题。不管涂不涂成白色，在加州强烈的阳光下，管道顶部的温度都会比底部高。也就是说，顶部膨胀得比底部厉害。对于一条500英里长的管道，就会产生严重的弯曲变形，就像双金属片上的情况一样。黄铜的膨胀程度理应大于钢。

cues.en: So the high metallic strip should bend toward the steel side. Your alternative, which probably has a better chance of working, is the 6000 vacuum seals. Although I've got to be honest. Vacuum seals on a 2 meter diameter tube. Speaking of someone who has decades of experience working with vacuums. I really don't rate your chances of that either.
cues.zh: 所以双金属片就会向钢的那一侧弯曲。你的另一个方案，也许成功的几率更高一点，那就是用6000个真空密封圈。不过实话实说，在直径2米的管道上做活动真空密封，作为一个有几十年真空领域工作经验的人，我觉得这种方案的成功率同样微乎其微。

cues.en: So why is this thing running in the vacuum anyway? Well that's easy, you cut down on the air resistance and this is the main reason why airplanes fly so high is because the atmosphere gets thinner the higher you get there's less air resistance however there is a compromise that your engines need that air to burn the fuel and create thrust so you can't go too high otherwise your engines run out of oxygen.
cues.zh: 那这东西为什么要在真空里运行呢？很简单，减少空气阻力。飞机飞那么高的主要原因，就是越高大气越稀薄，空气阻力越小。但这里有个取舍：发动机需要空气来燃烧燃料、产生推力，所以不能飞太高，否则发动机会缺氧。

cues.en: However, there's another problem. People also need air to live, so if there's any rupture in the hyperloop capsule for any reason whatsoever, you will die in the hyperloop in pretty much exactly the same way that you would die in deep space. You know, it's at times like this when I'm stuck in a vogue on airlock with a man from Betelgeuse about to die of asphyxiation in deep space that I really wish I'd listened to what my mother told me when I was young. Why would she tell you? I don't know! I didn't listen! And of course...
cues.zh: 不过还有个问题。人也需要空气才能活，所以不管什么原因，只要 Hyperloop 舱体出现任何破裂，你在 Hyperloop 里死去的方式，几乎和死在深空里一模一样。你知道，每当我跟一个来自参宿四的人一起被困在沃贡人的气闸里、即将在深空窒息而死的时候，我就特别希望自己小时候听了我妈的话。她跟你说了什么？我不知道！我没听！当然……

cues.en: People won't be able to hear you call for help, because as alien informals, in space no one can hear you scream. And that's essentially what the Hyperloop is doing. It's bringing all the impracticalities of space travel down to the surface of the earth and putting them inside a capsule, travelling at about the speed of sound in a giant gun barrel.
cues.zh: 没人能听到你呼救，因为正如《异形》所说：在太空里，没人能听到你的尖叫。而这本质上就是 Hyperloop 在做的事。它把太空旅行的所有不切实际之处搬到地球表面，塞进一个舱体里，让它在巨大的炮管中以接近音速飞行。

cues.en: So another one of the key problems is what happens when something goes wrong. If you're traveling at about a thousand kilometers per hour, the speed of sound in a capsule within centimeters or an inch or so of a tube, the velocity of the capsule is about that of a bullet fired from a gun, except it's a 15 ton bullet. Any failure whatsoever will rip through that two centimeter outer tube like candy.
cues.zh: 所以另一个关键问题是：一旦出故障会怎样。如果你以大约每小时一千公里——也就是音速——在一个距管壁只有几厘米或一英寸左右的舱体里行进，舱体的速度大约相当于枪射出的子弹，只不过这是一颗 15 吨重的子弹。任何故障都会像撕糖纸一样撕穿那层两厘米厚的外管。

cues.en: Now sure, anyone in that capsule will die pretty much instantly in the event of a crash, but then again, a car crash at 50 miles per hour will probably do that for you. The problem then comes that a single breach in the hyperloop will probably kill everyone else in the hyperloop. You see, once you've breached the outside tube, air will rush into the tube at about the speed of sound. Roughly this is how it works. The speed of sound is mostly determined by how quickly air molecules can actually knock into each other.
cues.zh: 当然，一旦发生撞毁，舱里的人基本上会瞬间死亡；但话说回来，每小时 50 英里的车祸大概也能要你的命。问题在于，Hyperloop 上只要有一处破损，可能就会杀死 Hyperloop 里的其他所有人。你看，一旦外管破了，空气会以大约音速冲进管道。原理大致是这样：音速主要取决于空气分子彼此碰撞的速度。

cues.en: which is basically how quickly the molecules are going. When they're moving into a vacuum, of course, there's nothing to stop them. So the air rushes into the vacuum basically at the speed of sound. Yeah, that will destroy any capsule it hits, and probably cause a cascade failure. I mean, ballpark numbers. There's a vacuum inside the tube, so the gas rushing into it is a pressure differential of one atmosphere.
cues.zh: 也就是分子运动的速度。当它们冲进真空时，当然没有什么能挡住它们。所以空气基本上会以音速涌进真空。没错，这会摧毁它撞上的任何舱体，还很可能引发连锁故障。我是说，粗略估算一下。管道内部是真空，所以冲进去的气体面对的压差是一个大气压。

cues.en: So what's it like getting hit by a pressure differential of one atmosphere? Well, let's take a look at it this way. Atmospheric pressure is about 10 tons per meter squared, about the size of a reasonable truck. And that one atmosphere pressure wave coming down the tube towards you is coming towards you at about the speed of sound. The only redeeming feature here is that air, gas, is pretty compressible stuff.
cues.zh: 那么，承受一个大气压的压差冲击是什么感觉？我们可以这样来看。一个大气压大约是每平方米10吨，差不多相当于一辆中型卡车的重量。而那股顺着管道向你袭来的一个大气压的压力波，正以接近音速的速度朝你扑来。这里唯一值得庆幸的是，空气这种气体具有相当大的可压缩性。

cues.en: but you can still expect it to kill pretty much anything it hits. I mean you get a rough idea of what a 1 atmosphere pressure wave will do from some nuke benchmarking tests.
cues.zh: 但即便如此，它撞上任何东西也基本是必死无疑。我是说，从一些核爆基准测试中，你就能大致了解一个大气压的冲击波会造成什么后果。

cues.en: The shock imparted by blast to the superstructure can damage or carry away equipment. At greater distances, overpressure above 6 PSI can distort, rupture, and carry away light structures and equipment. Interior equipment and compartments may be damaged by the blast, collapsing deck structures or bulkheads. Overpressure entering through openings can damage boilers. Blast injuries to exposed personnel represented by this dummy.
cues.zh: 爆炸对上层建筑施加的震波会损坏甚至直接掀飞设备。在更远距离上，超过6磅/平方英寸的超压就会使轻型结构和设备变形、破裂并将其冲走。爆炸还可能破坏内部设备和舱室，压塌甲板结构或舱壁。通过开口侵入的超压甚至会损坏锅炉。就像这个假人所代表的暴露在外的人员受到的爆炸伤害一样。

cues.en: is usually severe over 3 psi. Here it was 6 psi. Well, one of the methods by which they're going to power this is by a giant turbine on the front of the capsule, which is great, apart from they're running in a near-perfect vacuum, which means that our engine will have to spin astronomically fast, faster than it would if it was a terrestrial engine designed to run in our thick atmosphere. Engine is roaring along at full throttle. The blades spin at almost 3,000 revolutions per minute.
cues.zh: 在超过3磅/平方英寸时通常就很严重了，而这里达到了6磅/平方英寸。好吧，他们驱动这玩意的方案之一，就是在胶囊舱前端装一个巨大的涡轮机，这想法挺好，除了它们是在近乎完全真空的环境下运行，这意味着我们的发动机必须转得极其快，远比在浓厚大气层中运行的地面发动机快得多。发动机在全油门状态下轰鸣运转，叶片的转速接近每分钟3000转。

cues.en: The centrifugal force at the tip of each plane is equivalent to the weight of a 110-ton locomotive. I mean, dam are plane engines which are designed to run at about 30,000 feet, about 10 kilometres, run on about one-fifth of an atmosphere of pressure. That's 200 times higher than the pressure in the Hyperloop.
cues.zh: 每个叶片尖端承受的离心力相当于一辆110吨机车的重量。天呐，专为大约3万英尺（约10公里）高空设计的飞机发动机，是在约五分之一个大气压下运行的。而那也比Hyperloop里的气压高出了200倍。

cues.en: Now in the hyperloop of course you had 200 times less pressure than that which is great, that means you get 200 times less drag on your capsule. The downside of course is that your turbine will produce 200 times less thrust by actually spinning in that atmosphere than if it was a turbine spinning at about the altitude that a cruising jet flies at.
cues.zh: 当然在Hyperloop中，气压要比那低200倍，这很棒，意味着你的胶囊舱受到的阻力要小200倍。但缺点在于，你的涡轮机在这种稀薄大气中旋转产生的推力，也要比在喷气式客机巡航高度下旋转的涡轮机少200倍。
